licoes.objectivo: Rever as unidades 6 a 8 do C1.

exercicios.frase: Over fifty dollars? — I'm afraid [so].
I was [going] to keep it for Christmas.
Difficult [as] it is, that's the honest answer.
That, I'll [take] as a compliment.
We're on the verge [of] finishing.

opcoes.texto: This I can to promise you.

exercicios.enunciado: A supplier sends a 100-dollar bottle of whisky just before a negotiation. According to the policy, you…

opcoes.texto: declare it and send it back with a kind note

exercicios.enunciado: "Strictly speaking, it's a gift. In practice, it's a grey area." The speaker…

opcoes.texto: separates the letter of the rule from the real situation

exercicios.frase: I'm Lindiwe. In the morning, Marula wants to renegotiate. In the afternoon, a radio station wants to interview me.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Lindiwe have on Thursday?

opcoes.texto: a negotiation and a radio interview

exercicios.frase: This is Nuno. Think of it as a bucket that fills with sun. And one number: in five weeks, not one incident.
exercicios.enunciado: What number should Lindiwe give on the radio?

exercicios.frase: I'm afraid I can't promise lower bills. What I can promise is fewer power cuts in the evening.

exercicios.enunciado: A colleague has a negotiation and an interview on the same day. Give five pieces of advice, using one structure from each unit of C1.2 (ellipsis, an analogy or future in the past, fronting or a marker, register, negotiation).
exercicios.frase: Think of
exercicios.resposta: Send the gift back: strictly speaking, it's a grey area. On the radio, think of your project as a bridge. Expensive it may be, but say why it's worth it. Keep it simple, no jargon. And in the negotiation, find their interest and sum up every point.

exercicios.enunciado: Is honesty always the best policy in business? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: There are two ways
exercicios.resposta: There are two ways of looking at this. Short term, a small lie can win a deal. Long term, it destroys trust, and trust is what brings clients back. Where I come down is: yes, honesty is the best policy.

licoes.titulo: Review 2: register, the deal and the exam
licoes.objectivo: Rever as unidades 9 e 10 do C1 e praticar as estratégias do exame.

exercicios.frase: They offered a discount, but we turned [it down].
Thirty or [so] people came.
It's subject to the [board's] approval.
There are two ways of [looking] at this.
Much [depends] on the place.

exercicios.enunciado: "As nossas pretensões são razoáveis." Em inglês:

opcoes.texto: What we're asking for is reasonable.

exercicios.enunciado: In Part 3, the examiner plays a worried older client. Which opening fits?

opcoes.texto: Let's get the ball rolling, mate.

exercicios.enunciado: In Part 4, the examiner asks a big abstract question. A good start is…

opcoes.texto: There are two ways of looking at this.

exercicios.enunciado: Which of these does NOT lower your mark?

opcoes.texto: explaining a technical word in simple terms

exercicios.frase: I'm Lurdes. Two years ago, the bank was going to close our branch. Everyone thought it would happen within a year.
exercicios.enunciado: What was going to happen at the bank?

opcoes.texto: The branch was going to close.
The bank was going to open a new branch.

exercicios.frase: This is Lurdes. Where I come down is: close slowly, and keep one help desk in every town.

opcoes.texto: Close branches slowly and keep a help desk in every town.

exercicios.frase: There are two ways of looking at this. Much depends on the place. Where I come down is…

exercicios.enunciado: A hospital has money for one thing: more nurses, a new scanner, or a mobile clinic for villages. Choose two, compare them, speculate, and choose.
exercicios.frase: Of the three
exercicios.resposta: Of the three, the two I'd like to talk about are the nurses and the mobile clinic. I'd leave aside the scanner: it helps a few patients. More nurses means shorter waits. A mobile clinic, on the other hand, reaches people who never come. I'd go for the clinic.

exercicios.enunciado: Answer with structure: "Is technology making people more or less free?"
exercicios.frase: Much depends
exercicios.resposta: There are two ways of looking at this. Technology gives us choice, but it also watches us. Much depends on who controls it. Where I come down is: more free, if we understand it.
